sections.title: Living and Non-living Things
sections.explanation: Living things grow, need food, water and air, and can respond to the world around them. Non-living things do not grow or eat. Plants, animals and people are living; chairs, stones and toys are non-living. Sorting objects in your classroom and garden helps you practise this idea every day.
points: Living things grow and need food, water and air
Living things can reproduce (make more of their kind)
Non-living things do not grow or need food
Examples living: plant, cat, bird, fish, humans
Examples non-living: chair, toy car, stone, pencil

sections.title: Plants Around Us
sections.explanation: Plants are living things with parts that do special jobs. Roots take in water, the stem carries water and food, and leaves make food in sunlight. Flowers can lead to fruits and seeds. Trees are tall and woody; herbs are small and soft; climbers need support. Water your balcony plants and watch them grow after monsoon rains.
points: Roots take water from the soil
Stem carries water and food
Leaves make food using sunlight
Flowers can become fruits with seeds
Trees, herbs, shrubs and climbers are plant types

sections.title: Animals and Their Food
sections.explanation: Animals move to find food, water and shelter. Herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat meat, and omnivores eat both. Farm animals, pets and wild animals all have needs. Caring for a pet means giving food, water, love and a clean place — just like looking after friends.
points: Herbivores eat plants: cow, goat, rabbit, deer
Carnivores eat meat: lion, tiger, eagle
Omnivores eat both: bear, crow, humans
Pets need food, water, care and cleanliness
Animals live on land, in water or both

sections.title: Birds and Insects
sections.explanation: Birds have feathers, two wings and a beak. Many birds build nests and lay eggs. Insects are small animals that often have six legs; ants, butterflies and bees are insects. Bees help flowers, while some mosquitoes can spread sickness — so we use nets and keep water from collecting near home.
points: Birds have feathers, wings and beaks
Most birds lay eggs and many build nests
Insects often have six legs
Butterflies, ants, bees and houseflies are insects
Some insects help us; some can harm us

sections.title: Our Body and Senses
sections.explanation: Our body helps us play, learn and stay safe. The five senses — sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch — tell us about the world. Bones support us and muscles help us move. Sense organs must be cared for: protect eyes from sharp dust and never put small objects in ears or nose.
points: Eyes see; ears hear; nose smells; tongue tastes; skin touches
Bones give shape and support
Muscles help us move and play
Brain helps us think and remember
Keep sense organs clean and safe

sections.title: Food from Plants and Animals
sections.explanation: Food gives us energy to study and play. Some foods come from plants — grains, fruits, vegetables and dals. Some foods come from animals — milk, eggs, meat and honey. A balanced thali with different foods keeps us strong. Wash fruits from the market and drink clean water with meals.
points: Plant foods: rice, wheat, fruits, vegetables, pulses
Animal foods: milk, curd, eggs, meat, fish, honey
Eat different kinds of food for health
Drink clean water; wash hands before eating
Do not waste food from your tiffin

sections.title: Types of Houses
sections.explanation: Houses shelter us from sun, rain and wind. A kutcha house is often made of mud, straw or bamboo and may need repairs after heavy monsoon rain. A pucca house is stronger, made of bricks, cement and concrete. Igloos, tents and houseboats are special homes in different places. A clean house keeps the family healthier.
points: Houses protect us from weather and danger
Kutcha houses: mud, straw, bamboo, thatch
Pucca houses: bricks, cement, steel, concrete
Different places need different house styles
Keep homes clean and ventilated

sections.title: Uses of Water
sections.explanation: Water is precious for drinking, cooking, bathing, cleaning and growing plants. Animals need water too. We get water from taps, wells, rivers and rain. In hot Indian summers and during festivals we must not waste water. Saving water means closing taps and using a bucket wisely when possible.
points: We drink water to stay alive and healthy
Water is used for cooking, washing and cleaning
Farms and gardens need water for plants
Rain, rivers, wells and taps are water sources
Do not waste water; close taps tightly

sections.title: Air We Breathe
sections.explanation: Air is all around us even when we cannot see it. We feel air when the wind blows our school flag or dries clothes. Living things need clean air to breathe. Moving air is called wind. Smoke and dust can make air dirty, so open windows for fresh air and avoid burning plastic.
points: Air is invisible but we can feel it
We breathe air to live
Moving air is wind
Plants and animals also need air
Keep air clean; avoid smoke near children

sections.title: Weather, Day, Night and Seasons
sections.explanation: Weather tells us if a day is sunny, cloudy, windy or rainy. Day comes with sunlight; night is darker when we sleep. India has seasons such as summer, monsoon (rainy season) and winter. Clothes and activities change with weather — umbrellas in the monsoon and light cotton in summer heat.
points: Weather can be hot, cold, rainy or windy
Day is bright with the sun; night is darker
Monsoon brings much rain in many parts of India
Summer is hot; winter is cooler
Wear clothes that suit the weather

sections.title: Soil and Rocks
sections.explanation: Soil is the top layer of the ground where many plants grow. It holds roots and water. Rocks are hard pieces of the earth; small bits of rock mix into soil over a long time. Farmers need healthy soil for crops. We should not throw plastic into soil in parks or school gardens.
points: Soil helps plants grow
Soil holds water and nutrients for roots
Rocks are hard natural materials
Sand, clay and garden soil feel different
Keep soil clean; do not litter

sections.title: Materials Around Us
sections.explanation: Objects are made of different materials such as wood, metal, plastic, glass, cloth and rubber. Some materials are hard, some soft, some bendy. A steel tiffin is strong; a glass window can break if hit. Choosing the right material makes tools safe and useful at home and school.
points: Wood, metal, plastic, glass, cloth, rubber are common materials
Hard and soft materials feel different
Some materials are waterproof
Glass can break — handle carefully
Reuse and recycle when we can

sections.title: Pollution and Care for the Earth
sections.explanation: Pollution means making air, water or land dirty. Smoke, loud noise, plastic litter and dirty drains harm living things. Caring for the Earth means planting trees, saving water, using dustbins and saying no to wasting food and electricity. Even Grade 2 children can help by keeping the school ground clean after a fair.
points: Air, water and land can become polluted
Litter and plastic hurt animals and soil
Smoke makes air unclean
Plant trees and keep surroundings clean
Reduce, reuse, recycle as a family habit

sections.title: Safety, Hygiene and First Aid
sections.explanation: Safety rules protect us on roads, at home and in school. Cross roads with adults, stay away from fire and electricity, and never take medicines alone. Hygiene means washing hands, bathing and brushing teeth. First aid is simple help before a doctor comes — cleaning a small cut and telling a teacher right away.
points: Wash hands before eating and after toilets
Brush teeth and bathe regularly
Follow road safety with elders
Stay away from fire, sockets and unknown packets
For cuts: clean gently, cover if needed, call an adult
